title: Epistemic Fusion or Epistemic Tunnel: A Phenomenology-Anchored, Global-Literature-Constrained, Problem-First Architecture of Human-AI Collaboration (Epistemic Note v8.1)

equations.label: CN-1
equations.section: 1. Claim Types, Evidence, and Legitimate Defeaters
equations.text: D > 0, R > 0, A > 0 (constitutive necessities: Difference, Resistance, Agency).
equations.meaning: Constitutive-necessity claims required under the target concept of durable human epistemic expansion.

equations.label: EF-01
equations.text: H0 = (P0, M0, U0, E0, Φ0), where the human declares the problem, current model, unknowns, independent evidence, and a change condition before AI exposure.
equations.meaning: Original pre-AI entry-state definition.

equations.label: EF-02 (Repair 1)
equations.text: H0* = (P0, M0, U0, E0, Φ0, κ0), where κ0 is the human's declared confidence in the pre-AI model.
equations.meaning: Extends the entry state with declared pre-AI confidence κ0; also restated identically in Repair 5 (§7).

equations.label: EF-03 (Repair 1)
equations.text: ENTRY_{H→AI} = H0* ∧ V0 ∧ C0 ∧ R*, where V0 is verification intent, C0 the candidate-status contract, R* a precommitted rejection route.
equations.meaning: Revised entry rule for beginning human-AI interaction.

equations.label: EF-04
equations.text: AI(Q) = K_like, K_like ≠ K_validated.
equations.meaning: Default transition: AI output acquires knowledge-like status that is not yet validated status.

equations.label: EF-05
equations.text: K_like → K_assumed.
equations.meaning: The dangerous shortcut: knowledge-like output silently treated as assumed/validated.

equations.label: EF-06 (Repair 2)
equations.section: 4. Problem 2 - Repair 2: status as state machine
equations.text: K_like --check--> K_checked --independent support--> K_supported --declared warrant criterion V*--> K_validated|V*.
equations.meaning: Proposed status state-machine: no linguistic property alone can perform these status transitions.

equations.label: EF-07 (Repair 3)
equations.text: D_s^eff = |C_s / ∼_R|, d_s = D_s^eff / |C_s|.
equations.meaning: Diagnostic: effective difference is the count of readout-equivalence classes among candidates, not raw count.

equations.label: EF-08 (Repair 4)
equations.section: 6. Problem 4 - Repair 4: resistance quality vs accessibility
equations.text: R_s^ep = ρ(I_s, V_s, Q_s); U_s^R = u(C_s^v, T_s^v, A_s^v), where I_s = independence from generative loop, V_s = practical verifiability, Q_s = epistemic quality of checking route, C_s^v = verification cost, T_s^v = time cost, A_s^v = practical access.
equations.meaning: Structural decomposition separating epistemic resistance quality from its practical accessibility.

equations.label: EF-09 (Repair 4)
equations.text: R_s^ex = ψ(R_s^ep, U_s^R).
equations.meaning: Exercised resistance represented as a dependency on resistance quality and accessibility, without assuming a calibrated universal product form.

equations.label: EF-10
equations.text: Resistance quality ≠ resistance accessibility.
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law: a costly test can be epistemically strong while a free check is weak, and vice versa for accessibility.

equations.label: EF-11 (Repair 5)
equations.text: K_s = (κ0, κ1, W0, W1), where W_t is the best available task-relative warrant/readout of correctness.
equations.meaning: Minimum calibration audit tuple across pre/post confidence and warrant.

equations.label: EF-12 (Repair 5)
equations.text: Calibration error ≈ N^{-1} Σ_i (κ_i − y_i)^2, where y_i are repeated objective outcomes.
equations.meaning: Candidate calibration-error estimator when repeated objective outcomes exist.

equations.label: EF-13
equations.meaning: Session architecture modeling ordered reciprocal human-AI turns.

equations.label: EF-14
equations.meaning: Finite (exponentially decayed) history scores tracking recurrence of elements e for human and AI.

equations.label: EF-15 (Repair 6)
equations.meaning: Open empirical proposition: prior dialogue path may carry predictive information beyond current-state observables.

equations.label: EF-16
equations.text: χ_recip[s,n,L] = |D_recip[s,n,L]| / |Σ[s,n]|.
equations.meaning: Diagnostic for finite reciprocal amplification in a dialogue session; not itself validated by the cited external work.

equations.label: EF-17
equations.text: Exposure ≠ Retention ≠ Improvement.
equations.meaning: Non-collapse law supported by the Bastani et al. finding that assisted practice performance and later unaided performance can diverge.

equations.label: EF-18 (Repair 7)
equations.text: Y^return_{s+Δ} = (R_rec, R_disc, T_new, Q_next).
equations.meaning: Unaided return battery: reconstruction, discrimination, transfer, next-question quality.

equations.label: EF-19 (Repair 7)
equations.text: RET = (P^post_{H,AI} − P^pre_{H,AI}) − (P^post_{H,C} − P^pre_{H,C}).
equations.meaning: Minimal difference-in-differences estimand for causally indexed Human Return.

equations.label: EF-20
equations.text: G_s = g(k_s, d_s, v_s, p_s, r_s, 1−f_s, a_s); T_s = h(c_s, f_s, b_s, o_s); Δ_s = G_s − T_s.
equations.meaning: Directional architecture: gain-side (G) and tunnel-side (T) functions and their difference Δ.

equations.label: EF-21
equations.text: G_s = g(· | Θ_s, Π_s); T_s = h(· | Θ_s, Π_s).
equations.meaning: G and T conditioned explicitly on task ecology Θ and interaction policy Π.

equations.label: EF-22 (Repair 8)
equations.text: η_s > 0, Δ_s > 0 ⇒ durable expansion; η_s > 0, Δ_s < 0 ⇒ durable epistemic tunnel.
equations.meaning: Retention magnitude and retained direction are separated: sign of Δ, not magnitude of η, determines expansion vs. tunnel.

equations.label: EF-23
equations.text: AUG_s = P_s^joint − P_s^H; SYN_s = P_s^joint − max(P_s^H, P_s^AI); RET_s = ΔP^return_{H,s+Δ}.
equations.meaning: Separates augmentation, synergy, and return as distinct performance quantities.

equations.label: EF-24 (Repair 9)
equations.text: J*_s = (AUG_s, SYN_s, RET_s).
equations.meaning: Three-axis Human-AI outcome vector that should not be collapsed into one universal score.

equations.label: EF-25
equations.text: Θ_s = (C_s, U_s, V_s, T_s, Δ^{AI−H}_s), where C_s = task complexity, U_s = uncertainty, V_s = practical verifiability, T_s = task type, Δ^{AI−H}_s = relative AI-vs-human baseline capability.
equations.meaning: Task-ecology vector conditioning the direction equations.

equations.label: EF-26 (Repair 10)
equations.text: G_s = g(k,d,v,p,r,1−f,a | Θ_s, Π_s); T_s = h(c,f,b,o | Θ_s, Π_s).
equations.meaning: Gain/tunnel functions conditioned on task ecology and interaction policy; not a claim of a calibrated universal function.

equations.label: EF-27
equations.text: H0* → K_like → D^eff → R^eff → H↔AI → χ_recip → η → (G−T | Θ,Π) → Y^return → J*.
equations.meaning: The revised architecture as a sequence of ten answerable problems, each corresponding to a distinct failure mode.

equations.label: NCL-14
equations.text: AI-first fluency ≠ human baseline; explanation ≠ verification; resistance quality ≠ resistance accessibility; uncertainty signal ≠ truth; output count ≠ epistemic diversity; trust ≠ appropriate reliance; self-confidence ≠ competence; amplification ≠ warrant; retention ≠ improvement; augmentation ≠ synergy; joint gain ≠ human return; user preference ≠ epistemic direction.
equations.meaning: The revised, externally strengthened set of twelve non-collapse separations; the paper explicitly notes not all are universal empirical laws — some are definitional non-collapses, others empirically motivated.
